plugin.tls10-prf.title: TLS 1.0/1.1 PRF (P_MD5 ⊕ P_SHA-1)
plugin.tls10-prf.preset.tls10-master-sec: Master secret (NIST CAVP SP 800-135 TLS 1.0/1.1 case)
plugin.tls10-prf.param.md5MacHint: RFC 2246 fixes HMAC-MD5 for the first half. Another HMAC gives a different function, not the TLS 1.0 PRF.
plugin.tls10-prf.param.sha1MacHint: RFC 2246 fixes HMAC-SHA-1 for the second half. Another HMAC gives a different function, not the TLS 1.0 PRF.
plugin.tls10-prf.param.secretHint: 1 to 256 bytes: the pre-master secret for the master secret, the master secret for the key block. It is split into S1 and S2.
plugin.tls10-prf.param.label: Label
plugin.tls10-prf.param.labelHint: 1 to 64 ASCII characters, e.g. "master secret" or "key expansion".
plugin.tls10-prf.param.seedHint: 0 to 128 bytes, e.g. client_random ‖ server_random (64 bytes).
plugin.tls10-prf.param.lengthHint: 1 to 256 bytes. The master secret has 48 bytes.
plugin.tls10-prf.op.split: Split – cut the secret into S1 and S2
plugin.tls10-prf.op.seed: label ‖ seed – put the label in front of the seed
plugin.tls10-prf.op.a: A(i) – HMAC of the previous A
plugin.tls10-prf.op.p: P(i) – HMAC of A(i) ‖ label ‖ seed
plugin.tls10-prf.step.initial: The PRF starts from a {{secretLength}}-byte secret, the label "{{label}}" and a {{seedLength}}-byte seed, and produces {{length}} bytes. RFC 2246 fixes the two hashes: P_MD5 on the first half of the secret and P_SHA-1 on the second. This run uses {{md5Mac}} and {{sha1Mac}}.
plugin.tls10-prf.step.split: The {{length}}-byte secret is split in two: S1 is the first {{half}} bytes, S2 the last {{half}} bytes. Each half keys one HMAC.
plugin.tls10-prf.step.splitOdd: The {{length}}-byte secret has an odd length. S1 is the first {{half}} bytes and S2 the last {{half}} bytes, so both halves contain the middle byte (byte {{middle}}).
plugin.tls10-prf.step.seed: The label "{{label}}" ({{labelLength}} ASCII bytes) is put in front of the {{seedLength}}-byte seed. Both chains start from these {{total}} bytes (A(0)) and hash them again in every P block.
plugin.tls10-prf.step.aFirst: {{prf}}, block 1 of {{n}}: A(1) = {{mac}}({{key}}, A(0)) = {{value}}. A(0) is label ‖ seed itself.
plugin.tls10-prf.step.p: {{prf}}, block {{i}} of {{n}}: P({{i}}) = {{mac}}({{key}}, A({{i}}) ‖ label ‖ seed) = {{value}}. It becomes bytes {{from}} to {{to}} of the {{prf}} stream.
plugin.tls10-prf.step.xor: The first {{length}} bytes of {{md5}} and {{sha1}} are XORed. The result stays a pseudorandom function as long as either half is one: this hedges against a weakness in MD5 or in SHA-1.
plugin.tls10-prf.step.output: The {{length}} XORed bytes are the PRF output: {{output}}. P_MD5 computed {{md5Blocks}} blocks ({{md5Unused}} bytes unused), P_SHA-1 {{sha1Blocks}} blocks ({{sha1Unused}} bytes unused).
plugin.tls10-prf.derivation.title: TLS 1.0 PRF
plugin.tls10-prf.derivation.label: Label "{{label}}"
plugin.tls10-prf.error.invalidParams: Give the two HMACs, the secret, the label, the seed and the output length as text.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.md5Mac: Choose the HMAC for S1 from the list.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.sha1Mac: Choose the HMAC for S2 from the list.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.notHmac: {{id}} is not an HMAC. The TLS 1.0 PRF is defined over HMAC only.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.secretLength: The secret has {{length}} bytes; give 1 to 256.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.label: The label needs 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.seedLength: The seed has {{length}} bytes; give at most 128.
plugin.tls10-prf.error.length: Give the output length as a whole number of bytes from 1 to 256.
